slot.brief: Rank four alkyl/benzyl halides in order of SN1 reactivity, including one aryl halide and one tertiary halide with a rearrangement-prone neighbour.

stem: In the same solvent and at the same temperature, arrange these chlorides in increasing order of initial $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reactivity: chlorobenzene, 2-chloropropane, 2-chloro-2,3-dimethylbutane and 4-methoxybenzyl chloride.

verdicts.working: SN1 rate follows carbocation stabilization: chlorobenzene does not readily ionize; secondary isopropyl < tertiary alkyl; the para-methoxybenzyl cation is strongly resonance-stabilized and is fastest. Thus the order is A.

working:
Chlorobenzene: aryl C–Cl bond does not undergo ordinary $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ ionisation.
2-Chloropropane $\to$ secondary carbocation.
2-Chloro-2,3-dimethylbutane $\to$ tertiary carbocation.
4-Methoxybenzyl chloride $\to$ resonance-stabilised, methoxy-substituted benzyl carbocation.
Increasing reactivity: chlorobenzene < secondary < tertiary < 4-methoxybenzyl chloride.

Independent check: SN1 rate follows carbocation stabilization: chlorobenzene does not readily ionize; secondary isopropyl < tertiary alkyl; the para-methoxybenzyl cation is strongly resonance-stabilized and is fastest. Thus the order is A.
solution:
In an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction, reactivity increases with the stability of the carbocation formed. Chlorobenzene does not readily ionize; the other substrates form secondary, tertiary, and resonance-stabilized $p$-methoxybenzyl carbocations, respectively.
$$\text{Chlorobenzene} < \text{2-chloropropane} < \text{2-chloro-2,3-dimethylbutane} < \text{4-methoxybenzyl chloride}$$
